Maia for Accounting

All teams ↗

Coordinate the close around evidence

The close checklist may say an item is due, while the supporting document sits in a folder and the blocker lives in Slack. Maia can assemble those signals into a daily exception pulse. It helps the team see what needs attention without treating a summary as proof that an account is complete.

Provide the checklist, owners, due dates, and authorized evidence links. Ask Maia to show overdue items, missing support, and open exceptions. The controller decides whether evidence is sufficient and when a task can close.

Keep ambiguous matches unresolved

Reconciliation support starts with two defined record sets and explicit matching rules. Supply the matches produced by those rules, then ask Maia to organize clear candidates and records with no match or more than one plausible match.

The exception table should retain source identifiers, amounts, dates, and the rule applied. Maia's written summary is not the matching rule. An accountant validates each proposed match and resolves every ambiguous item in the accounting system.

Prepare invoice exceptions

For an accounts-payable review, supply invoice files or mailbox records, an approved AP export, and the policy that defines required fields. Maia can extract key details and group items with missing approvals, possible duplicates, or unclear payment status.

An invoice in email is not proof that it is unpaid. Payment status must come from the ledger or payment system, or remain unknown. The accountant confirms coding, approval, duplication, and treatment before any payment or record change.

Draft collection follow-up

Maia can prepare a collections queue from a confirmed aging export, customer details, known disputes, and prior correspondence. The result can show balance, due date, dispute status, last contact, and a draft follow-up.

The accounts-receivable owner verifies every figure and chooses how to handle the account. Any customer message stays a draft until an authorized person approves the content and sends it. Maia should not predict payment behavior or decide credit treatment.

Schedule a narrow close pulse

A routine can post a daily update during close when the source and rules are stable. Keep the report limited to changed status, missing evidence, and new exceptions. Include data timestamps so the team can tell whether an apparent blocker comes from a stale export.

Begin with a familiar checklist containing one ambiguous reconciliation item. Ask Maia to leave the item unresolved, attach both possible matches, and assign it to the accountant who can make the determination.

When a question is resolved, the thread can capture the evidence location, decision owner, and final status for the next close review. That record helps the team avoid reopening the same exception while leaving the formal accounting entry in its proper system.

Questions from accounting teams

Can Maia post journals or close the books?

This workflow prepares evidence and exceptions for review. Journal entries, period close, and accounting determinations stay with the accounting team in its approved system.

How does Maia handle PDFs?

Supply authorized files and ask for page citations. An accountant should verify extracted dates, amounts, and terms against the original document.

Can close updates run on a schedule?

Yes, for a bounded report with confirmed sources and recipients. Start with read-only status and keep completion decisions with the controller.
